title: Easy-to-Hard Generalization Characterization: Does Weak-to-Strong Transfer Work Better for Harder or Easier Targets?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct and compelling: easy-to-hard generalization is an explicitly listed open problem. Characterizing the difficulty threshold where weak-to-strong methods fail defines the safety boundary of these methods. High relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires constructing a difficulty ladder, running weak-to-strong fine-tuning at multiple levels, and measuring generalization at each. Fine-tuning multiple models is resource-intensive and technically complex for beginners even with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple interacting dimensions: constructing the difficulty ladder, fine-tuning at each level, measuring generalization quality. Each level is essentially a separate experiment. Very tight for 30 hours.
